From: Timothy Sanders <timothy.sanders@aurorahealth.com>

Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity pricing mechanics and GPU volatility

Marissa,

Thanks for taking my call earlier. As we push our inference footprint into production we need clarity on how Redwood thinks about long‑term reserved pricing when GPU spot/wholesale costs swing. Aurora is evaluating a 12–36 month committed pool; procurement wants to understand:

- Option structures you offer (fixed, indexation, slab + true-up)
- Typical discount bands and what requires executive approval
- Any pass‑throughs or caps tied to a GPU market index (we can provide sample index feeds)
- Contractual protections (credits, true‑ups, escrow) for sustained market shocks

Can you send an initial strawman and attach the financial model you referenced? We aim to present to finance next Wednesday.

—Tim
Timothy Sanders
Head of Cloud Procurement, Aurora Health
procurements@aurorahealth.com
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Timothy Sanders <timothy.sanders@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity pricing mechanics and GPU volatility

Timothy,

Appreciate the context — attached a short pricing model and three operational structures we typically offer for reserved capacity deals:

1) Fixed commit: fixed USD/unit price for the tenor (best predictability for customers, Redwood absorbs market moves; deeper discount for multi‑year but requires higher commit).
2) Indexed hybrid: base committed price + quarterly index true‑up tied to a GPU market index (we propose a +/- band and a maximum cap).
3) Slab + hedge credits: reserved slab with monthly true‑ups and an escrowed credit mechanism that pays back customers if realized GPU costs exceed modeled thresholds.

Quick notes on approvals: commercial discounts >25% generally need CRO approval; any contract clause that allows recurring downward adjustments >10% needs legal/finance review. Ive attached the CSV model and a sample SOW template.

Are you available for a 30‑minute call Thursday to walk the packet?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-05-04T11:36:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity pricing mechanics and GPU volatility — commercial ask and proposed numbers

Karthik / Priyom — looping you in. Aurora (large healthcare system) is evaluating a 12–36 month reserve. Highlights and my suggested defaults:

- Proposed commit bands: 12m = 15% discount; 24m = 22% discount; 36m = 30% discount (on list per-token compute rate).
- Market sensitivity: propose an indexation trigger if the GPU index moves >20% vs baseline for a rolling quarter. Trigger allows a capped true-up (max +10% pass-through to customer) or escrow credit in favor of the buyer if market costs are higher than modeled.
- Commercial governance: discounts >25% require CRO approval; any recurring downward price adjustments or credits need finance sign-off to confirm P&L impact.

Ask: Priyom, please propose contractual language for the Price Adjustment Mechanism and escrow mechanics. Karthik, confirm if we can approve 30% for 36m contingent on exec sign-off, and whether we should carve any SKU‑level restrictions.

Attached: redwood-pricing-model-v3.csv, Aurora_CAPEX_Schedule.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-10T09:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity pricing mechanics and GPU volatility — legal redlines

Marissa / Karthik,

Draft language below for the Price Adjustment Mechanism (PAM) — purpose is to limit exposure while providing operational predictability:

- Quarterly true‑up: At the end of each quarter, Redwood will compute actualized GPU cost delta using an agreed market index feed vs baseline modeled cost.
- Cap on pass‑through: A positive delta in GPU cost will not be passed through to the customer in excess of 10% of the contracted unit price in any single quarter.
- Escrow/credit: If cumulative delta across any 12‑month window exceeds 15%, Redwood will issue a credit applied to the next billing cycle equal to the delta above 15% (subject to maximum credit equal to 3 months of committed spend).
- Governance & audit: Aurora may request quarterly transparency reports and may engage an auditor annually to validate the index calculations (reasonable cost allocation applies).

Commercial approvals required: any effective discount that reduces forecasted ARR by >20% relative to list pricing requires exec review (CRO + CFO).

Ive added redlines to the SOW (attached) to reflect the PAM and audit rights. Finance needs to confirm the baseline cost assumptions used in the model (I flagged the GPU cost line item).

—Priyom
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOW-Aurora-Redwood-Reserved-2027-redlined.docx
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-20T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity pricing mechanics and GPU volatility — commercial approval path

Team,

Ive reviewed the ask and approve the following commercial guardrails:

- Approve 15% discount for 12m, 22% for 24m without exec sign-off.
- Approve up to 30% for 36m but require CRO sign-off for anything >25%.
- PCA (price change adjustment) clause: accept PAM language as drafted by Priyom, but change escrow cap to 4 months of committed spend (instead of 3) to make the offer more competitive for Aurora given their scale.
- Operational constraint: no more than 20% of reserved pool may be fungible across SKU families at the initial go‑live — limits risk of SKU misallocation if TPU/GPU mix shifts.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the thoughtful questions and the time this month. Summarizing the agreed commercial framework for Aurora:

- Commit options: 12m (15% discount), 24m (22% discount), 36m (30% discount; CRO approval required for final execution if discount exceeds 25%).
- Price Adjustment Mechanism (PAM): quarterly true‑ups vs agreed GPU index; pass‑through capped at +10% per quarter; escrow credit kicks in if 12‑month cumulative delta >15% (escrow max: 4 months of committed spend).
- Operational guardrails: up to 20% fungibility across SKU families at launch; SKU rebalancing requires 30 days notice and a quarterly review.
